answers.reasoning: Integral from 1 to 2 of 5x^4 is [x^5]_1^2=32-1.
The tangent slope is f'(1)=2(1)+1=3.
The secant slope is 1; f'(c)=2c=1, hence c=1/2.
Displacement is integral_1^3(4-2t)dt=[4t-t^2]_1^3=0.
Critical points are -2 and 0; values at -3,-2,0,1 are 14,-11,5,-2. Maximum plus minimum is 14-11=3.
f'(x)=4x^2(x-3); the only extremum is the minimum at x=3, with f(3)=-25. x=0 is stationary without an extremum.
At t=1, r=4 and dr/dt=2. dV/dt=4*pi*r^2*dr/dt=128*pi.
Split by roots 0 and 2. The areas on [-2,0] and [0,2] are 20/3 and 4/3, total 8.
Two distinct intersections require a repeated root. The difference cubic has critical x=1,3; positive k gives the double root at x=1 when k=2, with remaining root x=4.
Odd terms cancel because f is even; the remaining integral of f over [-1,1] is twice integral_-1^0 f=8.
For injectivity, f\u0027(x)=-3x^2+4ax+a must not change sign. Its discriminant is 16a^2+12a<=0, giving -3/4<=a<=0; the minimum is -3/4.
The functional identity forces F(x)=3x^2/2+cx+C. Since f=F' and f(0)=2, c=2; hence F'(-1)=-3+2=-1.
Factoring the linear polynomials f and g' using their sum -8x+9 and product -20x^2+54x-36, the integral identity and g(2)=7 select f=2x-3, g'=-10x+12. Thus g(3)=7+integral_2^3(-10x+12)dx=7-13=-6.
f'(x)=3x^2+12x+k has minimum k on [0,3], so the least k ensuring nonnegative derivative is 0.

Writing h=f-(4x+3), the two tangencies give h=((x-m)^2-1)^2. The condition for the line y=4x+4 gives the additional tangent at x=m and two intersections at m±sqrt(2). Since -3 is one of the roots of f\u0027-4, m=-2; then a=-2,b=-1, f(a)=-4 and f(b)=-1, product 4.
g'(2)=integral_0^2 f=16-4m+6n=0 gives m=4+3n/2, so n=2k,m=4+3k. For a local maximum f(2)<0 gives k>=2. m-n=4+k<=20 gives k<=16; 15 pairs.
Intersections are x=0,3. Area is integral_0^3[(-x+4)-(x-2)^2]dx=9/2.
A tangent at parameter t passes through (1,a) exactly when a=-2t^3+3t^2+1. This cubic has three distinct real preimages precisely between its local minimum 1 at t=0 and local maximum 2 at t=1.

The required root r in [1,3] must be double because |f| is differentiable there; the cubic is f=x(x-r)^2. With u=r-1 in [0,2], f(1)f'(1)=(1-r)^3(3-r)=u^3(u-2), whose maximum is 0 at the endpoints and minimum is -27/16 at u=3/2.
